# Chunk c04 - SUYU-GURecomp 35015f1 facts vs MHGU 1.4.0 disassembly

Scope: 3 blocks, all citing game_settings.cpp:1206 - 0x139de20, 0x139de4c, 0x139df40.
Note: SUYU "main+X" == our vaddr X. Own words only; no SUYU code copied.

| vaddr | meaning | SUYU cite | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x139DE20 | Interior address, not a function entry. Guarded virtual call: if the member at +544 is null the call is skipped (branch to 0x139deac); otherwise the byte flag at +596 is latched, the object is kept in r4, and the call is dispatched through the object's own vtable slot +0x38 with r0 = the object and r1 = the incoming r4. The member at +540 is stashed into r10 for use after the call returns. Shape matches one conditional call statement. | game_settings.cpp:1206 | PLAUSIBLE | `ldr r0, [r10, #544]` then `beq 0x139deac`; `ldr r2, [r2, #56]` then `blx r2` |
| 0x139DE4C | Continuation of the same statement immediately after the call returns (so the call and its uses share one source line). The latched byte in r11 picks the combine mode: nonzero -> OR of r9 with the result and require bit 0 set; zero -> AND of r9 with the result and require exactly 1. Failure jumps to the loop tail at 0x139df40; success at 0x139de70 restores the outer object from r4, sets r9 = 1, and builds an address from the stashed member (+540 plus 23). | game_settings.cpp:1206 | PLAUSIBLE | `cmp r11, #0` + `orr r0, r9, r0` versus `and r0, r9, r0`; `tst r0, #1` |
| 0x139DF40 | Interior address and a real branch target (both 0x139de60 and 0x139de6c jump here), i.e. the loop continuation / back-edge block. Clears a byte member at +1528 on the object in r6, restores the container pointer and the object pointer from stack slots, advances the index in r5, wraps it to 0 when it reaches the first count (container word +0), and repeats the body while it is not equal to the second count (container word +8). Net structure: a two-bound index walk, a nested iteration flattened onto one counter. | game_settings.cpp:1206 | PLAUSIBLE | `add r5, r5, #1` + `movge r5, r11`; back edge `bne 0x139dd58` |

## Notes / unknown

- The chunk supplies no SUYU source text for game_settings.cpp:1206, only address lists. Line-level binding therefore cannot be confirmed from the supplied material, which is why every row is PLAUSIBLE and none is VERIFIED; the structural reading of each address is taken from our disassembly and is solid.
- The 8-address list repeated verbatim under each of the three block headers is a per-function address set, not per-line data: it includes 0x139DDE0 (inside/at the head of the enclosing routine, outside all supplied windows) and 0x139E6E8/0x139E6F4/0x139E71C (far from our windows). 0x139DDE0 cannot be checked here because no window starts before 0x139de20.
- The function is clearly not a compiler-generated stub: it mixes a virtual dispatch, a byte-flag guard on +596, and a two-bound container walk. That is consistent with SUYU treating this address as the body of a settings-page routine whose loop/probe lives on one long source line.
- Observation, disassembly quality: 0x139de84 decodes as `strb r0, [r1, pc, lsl r0]`, a post-indexed store with pc as base and a register-controlled shift. The encoding 0xe7c1001f is valid ARM, but the rendering is fragile; if the analysis pipeline ever needs byte-exact replication of this block, re-check that single instruction in an independent disassembler.
- Observation, disassembly quality: the same window spells 0xe1550001 as `cmps r5, r1`, that is a plain CMP followed by the S-suffix spelling. Cosmetic only; no effect on the facts above.
- Not checked here: caller side of 0x139DDE0, and the code reached at 0x139deac, 0x139deb8 and 0x139dd58, all outside the supplied windows.
